items.title: 14.14 Strategies used to reduce air pollution

source_refs.note: Topic 14.14 as printed, with Figure 14.6, printed pages 317-318. The print announces five technologies and lists four.

blocks.text: A variety of technologies is used to reduce air pollution and improve air quality. The following five types of technologies we can be used to control emission of air pollutants.

Oxides of nitrogen and other undesirable gases such as CO and various unburnt hydrocarbon are emitted by the vehicle engines. The most cars are equipped with catalytic convertors to convert the harmful pollutants to harmless substances. CO is oxidized to CO₂. NOₓ are reduced to N₂. The unburnt hydrocarbon is converted to CO₂ and H₂O.

Diesel particulate filter (DPF) is incorporated in modern diesel engines to reduce the emission of harmful particulate matter (PM) from the exhaust gases. The primary function of diesel particulate filter is to capture and store soot particles from the exhaust gases.
SCR is used in diesel engines to remove pollutants from the emission gases. It reduces NOₓ to N₂ and oxidizes CO and hydrocarbons to CO₂ and water vapour using catalysts, such as TiO₂, zeolites, etc.

blocks.alt: Exhaust after-treatment line. From the Engine, an arrow carries NOx, CO, HC and PM into the Oxidation Catalyst, then a narrow pipe where a blue urea line enters at the Urea Dosing System (a green cone), then a wide can holding the Urea SCR block and the NH3 Oxidate Catalyst block. An arrow leaves with N2, CO2, H2O and PM.

blocks.text: Scrubbers can be used to control wide range of pollutants including particulate matters, SO₂, HCl, NH₃ and VOCs. Scrubbers use liquids (e.g. H₂O) to remove pollutants such as SO₂, PM from the industrial exhaust gases.
